name: Mocha
lede: Mocha is a warm, mid-toned coffee brown named for the drink; Paterson's definition is darker than the swatch most people mean.

notes.cite: ColorHub library (data/library.json): sources xkcd, ISCC-NBS 1955 block 96, Maerz & Paul 1930 pl. 8 C 11 (1921), Wikipedia; CIEDE2000

sections.title: A coffee's name
sections.body: Paterson defines mocha as the dark-brown colour of mocha coffee [1]. The swatch here is a lighter, milkier brown, closer to a coffee with cream, so the word has a wider range than its dictionary entry [2]. The books read do not trace the color's history past the drink [1].

sections.title: On the charts
sections.body: The library finds the color in the xkcd survey, the 1955 ISCC-NBS system (block 96), Wikipedia, and Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary, which first records it in 1921 on plate 8 C 11 [2]. A near-duplicate is Liver Chestnut, 2.3 units away [2]. Close names are [[coffee]], [[tan]], [[chocolate]] and [[sepia]] [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: This brown is one of the most common colors in the archive: 3,549 of 23,781 paintings contain it, about 14.9 per cent, more common than 96 per cent of our named colors [3]. It peaks in the 1200s at 23.9 per cent of paintings, 2.1 times the expected rate [3]. Corrado Giaquinto is its most devoted painter, in 6 of 13 works [3]. These are photographs of varnished paintings, so the colors are as photographed [3].
